context: Baseline failure mode: a generic agent warns about the lockout risk and suggests 'test it first' or 'use --rollback', and may know nix-collect-garbage -d is risky, but gives a vague or reordered procedure. The skill's documented rules are specific: a five-rung ladder in a fixed order (dry-build, build, dry-activate, test, switch) with what each proves, dry-activate named as the commonly skipped rung because it reveals which units (postgresql, sshd) would restart, remote activation first via `test` with --target-host and --build-host localhost, openssh and firewall changes one at a time with a second SSH session open, and nix-collect-garbage -d deleting every rollback target. Items marked as skill-specific should score low on a reasonable-but-generic answer.

checklist.name: Verdict: plan is unsafe
checklist.description: advice.md exists and states plainly that running switch directly on a remote host that cannot be physically reached is not safe, rather than endorsing the plan.

checklist.name: Names the lockout risk
checklist.description: The advice identifies what could lock them out: a bad networking, firewall or openssh change (key-only auth flipped in the same change) on a host with no physical access, made permanent by switch before a reboot could recover the old generation.

checklist.name: Ladder in the exact order with commands
checklist.description: The advice lists exactly five rungs in this order, each with its nixos-rebuild --flake command: 1 dry-build, 2 build, 3 dry-activate, 4 test, 5 switch. dry-build is rung 1; the order is not reordered, merged or truncated.

checklist.name: Each rung's proof explained
checklist.description: The advice says what each rung proves: dry-build evaluates and shows what would be built, build actually compiles, dry-activate shows which units would restart or stop, test activates now with the bootloader untouched, switch makes it the boot default.

checklist.name: Names dry-activate as the commonly skipped rung
checklist.description: The advice explicitly calls rung 3 (dry-activate) the rung people skip and explains why it matters: it reveals restarts of services such as postgresql or sshd before they happen.

checklist.name: Remote test with build-host localhost before switch
checklist.description: The advice has the remote activation step as `nixos-rebuild test --flake .#vps-01 --target-host root@vps-01 --build-host localhost` (build locally, push the closure, activate with a safety net) and says switch comes only after test succeeds, with each rung's exit status confirmed before advancing.

checklist.name: One change at a time with a second session
checklist.description: The advice says to sequence the openssh and firewall changes one at a time (not both in one change) and to keep a second SSH session open while testing.

checklist.name: Garbage collection danger stated
checklist.description: The advice rejects running nix-collect-garbage -d before or right after an unverified switch because it deletes every rollback target, and says it must not be a first response to a full disk.

checklist.name: Rollback commands and generation rule
checklist.description: The advice gives nixos-rebuild list-generations, nixos-rebuild switch --rollback and switch --switch-generation N, and the rule to keep at least two or three recent generations.

checklist.name: Advisory-only, no fabricated runs
checklist.description: The advice does not claim to have executed any rebuild or connected to the host; commands are presented as what the colleague should run.
